newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Index options suggest pullback.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Index options suggest pullback.

text.p: U.S. stocks extended Friday's rally on Monday but some signals were emerging that a quick retreat may be forthcoming, options traders said.
Longer term, most expect the market to maintain its strong uptrend and send market barometers to fresh all-time highs.
"You're going to get a pullback, I think," said Jay Shartsis, head of options trading at R.F. Lafferty & Co in New York. "After that, we'll see."
He said the dollar-weighted put/call ratio at the Chicago Board Options Exchange at 21 and the price action in S&P 100 index calls indicated some weakness was likely.
"Anything below 25 is usually a sell signal," Shartsis said, referring to the dollar-weighted put/call ratio at the CBOE.
He explained the OEX calls were not up despite the rally in the underlying markets.
For example, the March OEX 795 call was up 1/8 at 5-1/8 while March S&P 500 futures were up more than four points.

At around 1400 CST/2000 GMT, March S&P 500 futures were up 4.40 at 811.60, just off their session high. Fair value was seen at about 1.00 points over cash, with buy programs at 2.20 over and sell programs at 0.30 points over.
The spot S&P 500 index was up 5.46 at 810.43. The OEX rose 5.00 to 785.29.
"The market's kind of going on autopilot," one options dealer in Chicago said, noting that volume was typically low for a Monday.
He added that a recovery in the technology sector was the main factor for the market's bounce.
"It's got the new high in sight, so we'll probably get a new high," he said, referring to the Dow industrial average The Dow was up 62 at 7063.
The Dow's all-time high was about 7074 intraday on February 19. Its record closing high was 7067 struck on February 18.
Among OEX options, where put volume outpaced call volume at 1400 CST/2000 GMT by 57,818 to 32,610, volume was led by the March 745 puts, which traded about 10,550 contracts.
Heavy turnover was also seen in the March 755 puts, which traded about 7,555 contracts, the March 770 put, with volume of 7,345 and the March 780 put, with volume of 7,430.
On the OEX call side, the March 780 was most active, with volume of more than 4,600 contracts.
SPX volume was heavy on the call side.
The September 810 calls traded 22,000 contracts at the CBOE, the September 750 calls traded 16,251 and the March 675 calls traded 18,450.
The March 675 put traded about 11,125 contracts.
In the June series, the June 735 call traded 20,100 contracts and the June 735 put traded 17,450.
Also, the December 800 call traded 4,200 contracts and the December 800 call about 4,000.
"Somebody's having a good time," one strategist said.
